 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Andy Roddick has joined Serena Williams' coach Rennae Stubbs in criticizing Terence Atmane after the latter's outburst at the Shanghai Masters.
 Atmane faced Bernard Tomic in the first round of the qualifiers. He lost the first set 3-6. The Frenchman went on to put up a fight and clinched the second set, forcing a decider. As the match slipped away, Atmane became restless, and he hit a forehand into the net. Further, he smashed his racket on the net thrice. After an unforced error in the third set, Atmane threw his racket toward the crowd, which hit a metal bar but did not injure any spectators. He received a code violation for unsportsmanlike conduct and a point penalty.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Serena Williams' coach Stubbs shared a video of the incident on X and took a jibe at the umpire for poor judgement, demanding that Atmane be defaulted.
 "Honestly, who was the umpire here?" Stubbs wrote on X . "He should have absolutely been defaulted for this. To throw your racquet like that towards spectators and the only thing that saved them was the railing in front. ABSOLUTELY RIDICULOUS!"
 Andy Roddick also echoed his opinion with Stubbs, saying in the latest episode of his Served with Roddick podcast that Atmane's racket throw was dangerous as it nearly hit a spectator.
 "He's not someone I knew. He's not someone I have any connection to. I don't know his coach. There's not like an…honestly, when I've been around him, he's been really, really friendly, and I like talking to him about tennis. He asked… I like being around him.
I didn't like the US Open, this racket throw, and I've thrown rackets. I've been irrational. I've gotten point penalties. I'm not…I'm just saying. So, what he did with throwing a racket, where it was a very hard throw. He threw it 30 or 40 yards. Impressive throw. Threw it 30 yards, and it's six inches from hitting someone in the first row," Roddick said (from 10:16).
 Roddick compared Atmane's shocking reaction to Medvedev's and opined that the punishment should depend upon the action itself and not on whether someone actually gets hurt.
 "Compare that to what Medvedev did. I mean, where that ends up doesn't change the action," Roddick added. "And this is kind of my point from last week. That was as intense of a racket throw. And this might slide in front of the curious one at Indian Wells, where he threw it and almost hit the ball kid. That was…that, to me, it shouldn't matter if it hits the ball kid or not. The penalty should be the same. This doesn't matter to me. If you throw a racket and it hits the top bar of the stands or it's six inches higher and it hits a fan, in my mind, the penalty should kind of be similar. Yeah, the action should dictate over the result."
 Atmane eventually retired from the match, ending his Shanghai Masters run.
 Andy Roddick weighs in on Ben Shelton and Alexander Zverev's practice session controversy at the Shanghai Masters
 Andy Roddick recently addressed the controversy surrounding Ben Shelton and Alexander Zverev's practice session at the Shanghai Masters. Zverev faced heavy backlash from the tennis community after one of the fans alleged that he arrived late for a practice session in Shanghai. The spectator stated that Zverev showed up an hour late to his practice session and forced Ben Shelton and Cruz Hewitt to relocate. The fan also mentioned that the German player made his training partner wait for a long time.
 On his podcast, Andy Roddick's Served , the former World No. 1 called the allegations stupid and clarified that scheduling mix-ups during tournaments are common. He added that hitting partners (lower-ranked players) are hired to wait for opportunities to practice with top athletes.
 "If you're going to practice for a half hour, you're booking the court for an hour. You just are…and that's a warm-up. That's whatever else. You cannot make a peer wait for you to start practice. Unacceptable. I'm not going to wait around for 15 minutes because you just decided that you couldn't be out here on time. That would drive me absolutely crazy. Now, it is different if there, like, when I was 16 years old."
 "If it's a practice partner, someone literally they have people on site whose job is to wait around until someone wants to practice with them," Roddick added. "They signed up for that gig. Every tournament has those players who all they want is a chance to hit with—they wait around all day for a chance to hit with Vera, for a chance to hit with Moya, for a chance to hit with, you know, Andre or Serena if they need a body at the last second. Like there is an ecosystem for that. Their entire job is waiting and then hitting and then using the opportunity, right? So like don't pretend like you know how all of it works."
 Zverev has reached the semifinal round of the Shanghai Masters.
